title: Put a CompletableFuture in front of a callback FX client

blocks.text: The pricing service is moving to `CompletableFuture`, but its FX rates still come from a legacy client that takes a listener and answers later, on a thread of its own. A pricing request combines several rates with `thenCombine` and turns any failure into a "price unavailable" reply with `exceptionally`. Those requests must always get a reply: last quarter, a handler that waited on a rate nobody would ever deliver held its thread until the pool ran dry.

`Rates` declares the client's interfaces (don't change them) and `RateUnavailableException`. Finish `rate(pair)` in `src/main/java/practice/Rates.java`, so that it returns at once with a future that settles however the client's lookup ends: with the rate, or failed with a `RateUnavailableException` that carries the client's reason, or failed with whatever the client threw. Callers handle every failure through the future. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: rate() returns before the client answers, and the client's rate completes the future
two lookups answered in the other order each complete with their own rate
a failure the client reports through its callback fails the future with RateUnavailableException carrying the reason
a pair the client refuses on the calling thread gives a failed future, not an exception from rate()

origin.section: A Callback Adapter Must Complete the Future on Every Path the Legacy Call Can Take

concepts: A CompletableFuture made with new completes only when code completes it, so a callback adapter that ignores the legacy API's failure callback leaves its callers waiting forever.
An exception the legacy call throws on the caller's thread must become a failed future; otherwise it leaves the adapter past the caller's exceptionally.
